# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 73

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 8

---

## Disagreement 1 — "always feared God" vs. "have always feared God"

- **EMET:** "always feared God"
- **LOGOS:** "always feared God"
- **PNEUMA:** "have always feared God"
- **Greek:** *aei ton theon ephobēthēsan* — "always feared God"
- **Ruling:** All agents render essentially the same; PNEUMA uses perfect tense. SOPHIA uses "always feared God" (EMET/LOGOS). Simple past is consistent with the aorist *ephobēthēsan*.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "did not swerve" vs. "did not deviate" vs. "never wavered"

- **EMET:** "did not swerve at any point"
- **LOGOS:** "did not deviate in any way"
- **PNEUMA:** "never wavered in any way"
- **Greek:** *mēden exeklinan* — "deviated/turned aside nothing/at all"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "did not deviate in any way" (LOGOS). *Ekklinō* means "to turn aside/deviate" — "deviate" is the most literal; "swerve" is vivid but slightly informal; "wavered" suggests uncertainty rather than moral deviation.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "live for God" vs. "live to God"

- **EMET:** "they will live to God"
- **LOGOS:** "they will live for God"
- **PNEUMA:** "they will live for God"
- **Greek:** *zēsontai tō theō* — "they will live to/for God"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they will live for God" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). "Live for God" is the standard English idiom; "live to God" is more literal but slightly archaic.

---

## Disagreement 4 — "full of compassion" — all agree

- **EMET:** "full of compassion"
- **LOGOS:** "full of compassion"
- **PNEUMA:** "full of compassion"
- **Greek:** *polysplanchnos* — "many-boweled / deeply compassionate"
- **Ruling:** All agents agree. No ruling needed. SOPHIA retains "full of compassion" as the established rendering of *polysplanchnos*.

---

## Disagreement 5 — "grant repentance" vs. "give repentance"

- **EMET:** "give repentance to all"
- **LOGOS:** "grant repentance to all"
- **PNEUMA:** "give repentance to all"
- **Greek:** *dounai metanoian pasin* — "to give repentance to all"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "grant repentance to all" (LOGOS). "Grant" carries the sense of authoritative bestowal, appropriate to a divine commission; "give" is accurate but less precise.

---

## Disagreement 6 — "strive well" vs. "struggle well" vs. "keep fighting"

- **EMET:** "struggle well"
- **LOGOS:** "strive well"
- **PNEUMA:** "keep fighting"
- **Greek:** *kalōs agōnizou* — "strive well / compete well / fight well"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "strive well" (LOGOS). *Agōnizomai* is the athletic/combat verb used by Paul (1 Tim 6:12; 2 Tim 4:7). "Strive" captures both the effort and the purposefulness; "keep fighting" (PNEUMA) is too casual.

---

## Disagreement 7 — "was laughing" vs. "laughing"

- **EMET:** "he was laughing as he departed"
- **LOGOS:** "as he departed he was laughing"
- **PNEUMA:** "he was laughing"
- **Greek:** *gelōn apēlthen* — "laughing, he departed"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "as he departed, he was laughing" (LOGOS). The participial construction should be rendered with the temporal relationship preserved; LOGOS achieves this most clearly.

---

## Disagreement 8 — "The Lord has not forgotten me" — PNEUMA adds "hasn't"

- **EMET:** "The Lord has not forgotten me"
- **LOGOS:** "The Lord has not forgotten me"
- **PNEUMA:** "The Lord hasn't forgotten me"
- **Greek:** *ouk epelatheto mou ho kyrios* — "the Lord has not forgotten me"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "The Lord has not forgotten me" (EMET/LOGOS). The uncontracted form is appropriate for a solemn theological declaration.

---

*Disagreement log generated 2026-03-17. SOPHIA rulings are binding for the consensus text.*
